reader.requirement: An indexed file's FD takes the Sequential I-O RECORD clause whole (VII.3.8): format 1 RECORD CONTAINS integer-1 [CHARACTERS] (SR1: no record description larger than integer-1), boxed format 2 RECORD IS VARYING [FROM i2] [TO i3] [CHARACTERS] [DEPENDING ON d] (SR2 bounds, SR3 i3 > i2, SR4 d elementary unsigned integer in WS/Linkage; GR8-GR12 write length from d or the ODO, status 44 out of range, READ sets d, DELETE/START/failed READ leave d alone, READ INTO sends the record's length) and format 3 RECORD CONTAINS i4 TO i5 (no syntax rule; GR14 sizes come from the descriptions); no BYTES word at 1985. Witness g85_f17_08 covers format 1 and format 2 GR11 only.

reader.notes: The pointer rule's range is the whole Sequential I-O RECORD clause applied to an indexed file; every syntax rule and the run-time general rules probed behave per the 1985 text, with the 1985-only arms (no BYTES, unordered and non-binding format 3) taken by edition switches. GR2 (external connector consistency) was not probed: it states a program obligation across run units.

refuter.evidence: occ2.cob (refute-1985-093/occ2-001): FD XB RECORD IS VARYING IN SIZE FROM 4 TO 12 CHARACTERS DEPENDING ON XB-TL, where XB-TL is 05 PIC 99 OCCURS 2 under a WS group. --std 85 compiles clean (EXIT 0) and runs: XB-TL(1)=13 then WRITE gives 'W 00' (GR10a would make it unsuccessful, 44), and after a successful READ 'R 00 T1 00 T2 00' (GR11 sets no occurrence): the DEPENDING ON operand is silently disregarded. Same at --std 2023. The 1985 format's data-name-1 is a data-name, which 'must not be reference-modified, subscripted, or qualified unless specifically permitted' (cite.py: OK §1985:III, the text is in the clause), and a table element reference must be subscripted (cite.py: OK §1985:IV.4.3.8.2.3 SR4), so a table element cannot be data-name-1; the SR4 screen (cite.py: OK §1985:VII.3.8.3 SR4) tests only elementary/unsigned-integer/section. Sibling contrast: occ3.cob FILE STATUS naming an OCCURS item is refused COBOL2455. Also ran sr4ed (Z9), sr4dec (9V9), sr4x (XX): COBOL2922 correctly; sr4p (9PP, an integer), sr4comp, sr4lvl77: admitted correctly. cite.py OK §1985:VII.3.8.4 GR11.

adjudication.reason: `RECORD VARYING ... DEPENDING ON TL`, TL an element of a table, compiles, and at run time the length is ignored (a WRITE gives 00 where an elementary item gives 44). The subscripted spelling is refused. 2023 rows `FMT-13.18.43.2` and the operand rule `SR-13.18.43.3-6`.
